statistics of all generic, classically chaotic systems are related to those of the RMT ensembles (COE
for time-reversal symmetric integer-spin systems, CUE for non-time-reversal integer-spin systems,
and CSE for half-integer-spin systems) [10], and our results might then be expected to apply to
the corresponding quantum spectral determinants. It is worth noting in this respect that extensive
numerical evidence supports the conclusion that for classically chaotic systems the value distribution
of the uctuating part of the spectral counting function (which is proportional to the imaginary
part of the logarithm of the spectral determinant) tends to a Gaussian in the semiclassical limit
[6, 2].

before.text:
Katz and Sarnak [22, 23] have conjectured that correlations between the zeros low down on the
critical line, de ned by averaging over L-functions within certain particular families, are described
not by averages over the CUE, that is, over the unitary group U (N ), but by averages over other
classical compact groups, for example the orthogonal group O(N ) or the unitary symplectic group
USp(2N ). Thus the value distributions within these families close to the symmetry point t = 0 on
the critical line will also be described by averages over these families. We shall present our results
in this case in a second paper [26].

unit_result_entry.why_material: Fourier inversion gives a large-N lognormal-type bulk approximation, while the nearest pole controls the fixed-N near-zero limit; the source explicitly diagnoses why exchanging the N and w limits invalidates the bulk approximation.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The figure is supporting calibration; the reusable mechanism is the saddle-versus-pole and nonuniform-limit distinction.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A separate arithmetic product corrects phase moments and matches low-order checks
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Constructs the phase analogue of the multiplicative model, reports improved finite-height moments, and checks consistency with the second-moment formula and independent low-order heuristics.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The arithmetic product affects near-zero and tail probabilities more than the bulk
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Multiplies the magnitude transform by the arithmetic factor, checks the near-zero correction numerically, and uses the saddle location to explain why the prime contribution is pushed toward the tail for large N.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Fourier/Mellin inversion links analytic generator structure to distributional regimes: a saddle controls the bulk, the nearest pole controls fixed-N near-zero values, and the arithmetic multiplier is most visible away from the large-N bulk.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The approximations are nonuniform in N and magnitude, so exchanging limits or extending the saddle formula to the origin is invalid.
